record.title: Anthropic says UK AISI declined restricted pre-release access to Mythos 5.1; access later resumed
record.summary: In UK Parliament evidence on October 13, Anthropic’s Head of EMEA Policy said the company could not provide UK AISI with full, unrestricted pre-release access to Mythos 5.1, but had offered restricted access, which AISI chose not to use; he said AISI had access to the model by the hearing. Asked whether the difference was Anthropic’s decision or driven by the US Government, he said he did not know and had not been privy to those conversations. In an October 22 follow-up letter published October 27, Anthropic repeated that it could not provision unsafeguarded access while a new US framework for pre-deployment testing and access was being considered, and said it later provisioned unsafeguarded access to its latest models. These are Anthropic’s accounts. They establish an offered restricted-access path and later access, but not the reason or the exact scope and duration of the restriction.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Anthropic’s representative told Parliament on October 13 that Anthropic could not provide UK AISI with full, unrestricted pre-release access to Mythos 5.1, offered restricted access instead, and that UK AISI chose not to use the restricted offer. He said UK AISI had access to the model by the hearing.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Anthropic’s representative said he did not know why US and UK access differed and was not privy to the relevant US-government conversations.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In its October 22 follow-up letter, Anthropic said that while governments considered a new US framework for pre-deployment model testing and access, it could not provide unsafeguarded pre-deployment access to Mythos 5.1; it said it later provisioned UK AISI with unsafeguarded access to its latest models.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The UK Parliament published the oral-evidence transcript and Anthropic follow-up correspondence; the records identify the hearing date as October 13 and the letter date as October 22, published October 27.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The inspected official records do not establish that the US Government ordered or caused the restriction, nor specify its exact start date, terms, or duration.

evidence_gaps.description: A direct UK AISI or US government account is needed to clarify the decision-maker, reason, precise conditions and timing of the restricted access offer.
The records do not specify the access controls attached to the restricted Mythos 5.1 offer or the model versions covered by later unsafeguarded access.

brief.importance_rationale: If restrictions on independent pre-release evaluation persisted across frontier systems, they could materially affect cross-border safety oversight. The official record describes a restricted offer that UK AISI declined and says access was later available; it does not establish a lasting policy shift or its cause.
limitations: Access history, the offered restricted path, UK AISI’s decision, and later access are reported by Anthropic, not independently verified by UK AISI or the US Government.
The Anthropic representative said he did not know why US and UK access differed and was not privy to US-government conversations; the evidence does not establish a US government order or causal role.
The exact dates, technical scope and safeguards of the restricted offer, and whether later access was equivalent to earlier pre-release testing, are unspecified.
This episode does not show that the UK lost all Anthropic access or that external evaluation changed model safety.
brief.summary: In UK Parliament evidence on October 13, Anthropic’s Head of EMEA Policy said the company could not provide UK AISI with full, unrestricted pre-release access to Mythos 5.1, but had offered restricted access, which AISI chose not to use; he said AISI had access to the model by the hearing. Asked whether the difference was Anthropic’s decision or driven by the US Government, he said he did not know and had not been privy to those conversations. In an October 22 follow-up letter published October 27, Anthropic repeated that it could not provision unsafeguarded access while a new US framework for pre-deployment testing and access was being considered, and said it later provisioned unsafeguarded access to its latest models. technical.claimed_result: Anthropic’s representative told Parliament that UK AISI was offered restricted pre-release Mythos 5.1 access, chose not to use it, and later had access; Anthropic’s follow-up letter says unsafeguarded access to its latest models was later provisioned.
technical.demonstrated_result: The UK Parliament transcript and follow-up letter are publicly available and directly record Anthropic’s statements, including that its representative did not know the US/UK access rationale. The underlying access arrangements are not independently verified.
technical.mechanism: Pre-deployment testing access is a form of third-party evaluation capability. The letter describes a temporary difference between safeguarded and unsafeguarded access for one model while government discussions about a US testing/access framework were ongoing; it does not give the decision rule or identify the decision-maker.
technical.regime: Anthropic models and UK AISI pre-deployment testing; one Mythos 5.1 access interval, with later access described only as for “our latest models.”
technical.reproducibility: Not applicable to this correspondence event; access status and causation were not independently verified.
technical.strongest_baseline: Anthropic says it provided UK AISI early safety-research access since 2023 and pre-release testing access since 2024; by the October 13 hearing it said UK AISI had access to Mythos 5.1. No direct UK AISI or US government account was inspected.

brief.title: Anthropic says UK AISI declined restricted pre-release access to Mythos 5.1; access later resumed
brief.why_it_matters: Pre-release access affects whether external safety institutes can inspect frontier models before launch and under what conditions. The official record narrows the story: UK AISI was offered restricted access to Mythos 5.1 and declined it, then had access by the October 13 hearing. This does not establish a US government order, a lasting exclusion, or an effect on model safety.
